body: ## Summary The white-label logo is stored as a URL and re-fetched from the owner's host on every PDF download and every anonymous share view. Make it an asset: at save time one pinned, format-sniffed fetch produces a snapshot (data URI + sha256 + sourceUrl) in its own table, and both client-facing deliverables read the snapshot through one entitlement-checked door. The render path stops making network calls, the DNS-rebinding window closes, an unsupported format is refused at save instead of silently unbranding the PDF, and board viewers stop beaconing a third-party host. ## Description - `src/lib/net/pinned-get.ts`: a dependency-free HTTPS GET (`node:https` with a `lookup` option that returns the single address validated by `isPrivateOrInternalHost`), no redirects, timeout, byte cap. This is the resolve-and-pin the branding.ts:32 comment defers. - `src/lib/net/logo-fetch.ts`: `fetchSafeLogo(url) -> {ok, bytes, mime, sha256} | {ok:false, reason}` over pinned-get; sniffs magic bytes and admits exactly the formats @react-pdf/image renders (png, jpeg, svg) at <= 512 KB. `resolveSafeLogoDataUri` stays as a thin wrapper so no other caller changes. - `OrgLogoSnapshot` table (orgId PK, sourceUrl, dataUri TEXT, sha256, mime, status ok|failed, reason, fetchedAt). Its own table so the hot Organization row never carries a 700 KB string; TEXT not bytea per the schema's DSQL-safety contract. `src/lib/db/org-logo-snapshot.ts` reads/writes it. - `POST /api/org/branding`: the save-time probe becomes the snapshot (one fetch, not a probe then a second fetch at render); `logoUnreachable` now also covers unsupported formats. - `src/lib/branding/deliverable.ts` `readDeliverableBranding(org)`: entitlement re-check (planAllowsWhiteLabel, unchanged semantics) -> branding -> snapshot when `sourceUrl` matches, else heal once (pre-migration rows, or a URL changed outside the form) with a 1 h negative cache. PDF route and share page call it; the share page's `` now gets a same-document data URI. - PDF fallback ladder: branded -> branded without logo -> unbranded, so a logo failure never strips the brand name and accent. What is paid for does not change: the door applies the same `planAllowsWhiteLabel(credit?.plan)` check both call sites apply today, and a downgraded org still gets no branding. Sanitization only tightens (pinned connect, magic-byte sniff, smaller cap); no URL or CSS is newly accepted. ## Flow - Owner saves logo URL -> literal-host SSRF check (unchanged) -> pinned fetch -> sniff -> snapshot row -> response warns if not ok. - Board member opens share link / owner downloads PDF -> readDeliverableBranding -> snapshot data URI -> render, zero egress. - Legacy org with logoUrl and no snapshot -> first render heals once -> cached. ## Expected impact Render-time egress to owner-supplied hosts goes from 1 per PDF download and 1 per share view to 0 (only save and heal). The rebinding TOCTOU named at logo-fetch.ts:22 closes. A WebP/GIF logo is refused with a reason at save instead of yielding a PDF that loses its whole brand. One door replaces two hand-copied entitlement re-checks. Applies registry settings > save-experience ('what you see here is what the system will do') and the one-validation-door law; governance on this context is weak, so the egress part leans on the existing SSRF conventions rather than a registry subject. ## Evaluation Claim: the deliverables render the logo the owner saved, from a pinned, sniffed snapshot, with no render-time network call and no loss of name/accent on a logo failure. Before: 0 of 8 cases pass After: 8 of 8 Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first Result: better Gate: architecture (new cache table + init.sql mirror; additive, droppable)

body:
## Summary
Today the branding form only finds out what the server thinks after it has saved, and saving a bad logo URL overwrites the working one with null. Add a no-write check endpoint with the same gate as the save, debounce it under the form, and show a per-field verdict (with the reason), a preview that only shows a logo the PDF will really get, and a Save button that names what it is about to destroy.

## Description
- `src/lib/branding/normalize.ts`: the pure normalization `setOrgBranding` runs today (trim/80-char name, hex colour, https + public host + <= 500 chars logo), plus a `reasons` map. `setOrgBranding` calls it, so the save and the check cannot drift (one-validation-door).
- `POST /api/org/branding/check`: `requireOrgOwnerPost` + `refusePublicOrgAdmin` + `planAllowsWhiteLabel` (503 on plan read failure), exactly the POST's gate. No write, no audit. Returns normalized values, rejections with reasons, an optional logo reachability verdict from the existing `resolveSafeLogoDataUri` (`probeLogo` only when the URL changed), and contrast on both surfaces. It never echoes fetched bytes.
- `useBrandingCheck.ts`: 600 ms debounce, abort/stale-drop, probe-only-on-logo-change.
- `brandingVerdictModel.ts`: pure; maps (stored, draft, verdict) to field notes, a preview logo state and a save intent: plain / warn / destructive ('Save and remove the current logo').
- `BrandingVerdict.tsx` renders the notes in both the Altimeter and Prism forms; `BrandingPreview` hides the browser-loaded image when the server says the PDF won't have it.

Nothing about what is paid for changes: the check is Team+ and owner-only like the save. No validation rule is loosened; the check reports the existing rules earlier.

## Flow
- Owner types a logo URL -> 600 ms later the form shows 'Must be an https URL' or 'Didn't return an image, so the PDF would have no logo' next to the field -> preview shows 'No logo in the PDF' -> Save reads 'Save and remove the current logo' -> owner fixes the URL before anything is overwritten.

## Expected impact
The decision the owner makes blind today (save, then discover the drop) becomes a decision made with the server's own verdict in front of them. A mistyped URL no longer silently deletes a working logo. Applies registry settings > save-experience (honest feedback: what you see is what the system will do; never a green state for a write that changed something else).

## Evaluation
Claim: every rejection or unreachable logo the save would produce is visible, with its reason, before the save, and the save button names the destructive case.
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: contract (new read-only owner endpoint, same gate as the write)

body:
## Summary
Playbook lift is the number the Practices card and the executive briefing's proof line print as evidence a standard worked. Today it is computed from the org's whole scan history, counts mock scans, and puts the landing scan (which already contains the playbook) on the baseline side. Move the pairing into a pure model with a closed status set and read exactly two scans per application through the latest-scan door.

## Description
Registry: software-engineering / adoption-measurement, technique before-after-outcome-pairing (steps 4, 5, 6, 7): resolve the boundary toward 'after', compare only what both sides scored, emit a named status for every attempt, report the unpaired population beside the delta. The current reader violates 4 (playbook-adoption.ts:138 `<=`), 6 (failed pairs are silently dropped) and 7 (only `measured` travels). It also re-opens the exact whole-history transfer that today's rollups door closed for every org-*.ts reader, from a file the guard does not scan.

## Flow
- playbook-lift.ts: per application round (at most one application per repo per round), `latestScanAtPerRepo` for the reading at-or-before the instant when the mark is scan-stamped, `scanAtBeforePerRepo` for the strict-before reading, the latest per repo, then one `atPairs` fetch selecting engineProvider + the playbook dimension only.
- playbookLiftModel.ts (pure): pair(application, before, after) -> paired | no-before | no-after | mock-reading | no-dimension; fold to { lift, measured, unpaired }; liftSampleNote for the card.
- getPlaybookAdoption keeps its signature and adds the optional `unpaired`.
- PlaybookCardAdoption's lift title uses liftSampleNote.

## Expected impact
The proof line stops crediting or debiting a playbook with the score of a scan it already shaped, mock scores stop entering a published lift, and the read is constant in history depth instead of linear.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - lift is a before/after pair with a stated unpaired population, read in O(applications) rows
Before: 0 of 6 cases pass
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: contract (PlaybookAdoption gains an optional field; displayed lift numbers change for scan-stamped marks and mock-latest repos, and practices.md must say so)

## Summary
An org edits its playbook to v3. The card says v3. Every repo that adopted v1 stays on v1 forever: re-applying is refused because the landed file exists on the default branch, and a title edit would seed a second file. Add a 'behind' set and a capped, admin, typed-confirm revision rollout that replaces only a file whose bytes are exactly what Ascent saw land.

## Description
This is the playbook half of the 're-convergence' the practices library has for house patterns (practices.md 'Reuse doesn't update' closed for house patterns only). Registry: software-engineering / versioning-snapshots (an adoption cites the version it landed) and adoption-measurement (count-carries-predicate). The overwrite guard's invariant is kept for every caller and narrowed for one: never replace a base file whose content Ascent did not itself land. A hand-edited (drifted) file is never offered and the write refuses it anyway, because its digest no longer matches.

## Flow
- playbookRevisionModel.classify per (repo, ledger row, appliedVersion, playbook version) -> behind | diverged | unversioned | current | in-flight.
- playbook-revision.ts lists the sets and stamps appliedVersion on a rebaseline.
- revise route: GET member, POST admin, dedupe then cap 25, dryRun, archived 409, every coordinate must be in the behind set, audit `playbook.revision_opened` with the version span.
- applyPlaybookToRepo revision mode: path from the ledger, replaceIfBaseDigest = ledger adoptedHash, ledger patternVersion = playbook.version.
- reconcile: adopted + census == proposedHash -> rebaseline, then appliedVersion = patternVersion.
- PlaybookRevisionRollout on the card: 'N repos on v1-v2 -> update to v3', preselected, confirm naming org + repos.

## Expected impact
Editing a standard stops being a silent fork between the library and the fleet; an admin sees who is behind and closes the gap in one confirmed action, and the adoption ledger keeps telling the truth after the revision lands.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an edited playbook can reach the repos on its older version
Before: 0 of 6 cases pass (re-apply to an adopter 409s)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better

## Summary
The register on the landing page puts repos in one numbered order, but each number was weighted under that repo's own archetype lens (solo, team or org), and the lenses disagree by up to 2x on a dimension. The deck explains lenses only as a static weight table (DimensionMatrix), so the visitor ranks a solo library against a platform monorepo without knowing, and cannot see what the lens they would be scored under does to a real repo. Add a lens switch to the register: 'As scored' (today's board, plus a 'rows weighted under N lenses' note) or Solo / Team / Org, which re-weights every live row in the browser with the engine's own overallScoreFor and shows each row's rank move.

## Description
A pure model, registerLensModel.ts, takes the board cards and a lens and returns rows {card, score, level, rank, move, reweightable} plus lensesOnBoard and withheld. A row is re-weightable only when the engine's function reproduces its stored overall under its own archetype, so the page never prints a recompute that disagrees with the report the row links to; others stay on the as-scored board and are counted, not re-ranked. RegisterLensSwitch.tsx is a four-button aria-pressed group; IndexGallery holds the lens in state, renders the model's rows, keeps the rubric chip and links, and adds one line saying the figures are re-weighted in the browser and each report keeps its own score. The switch only appears on a ranked board.

## Flow
- Visitor reaches The register, sees 'As scored - rows weighted under 3 lenses'
- Clicks 'Solo' (the lens their single-author repo would get) -> rows re-order, moves marked, scores re-weighted
- Clicks a row -> its report, which shows the score it was actually scored under
- Back to 'As scored' -> today's board exactly

## Expected impact
The lens stops being an abstract table and becomes something the visitor can test on real repos before scanning their own, and the register stops implying that numbers from three weightings are one scale.

## Evaluation
Claim: the register can be read under one lens, with every re-weighted figure reproducible by the engine's function
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: none. Registry: software-engineering/peer-benchmarking, technique comparability-filters (a weight-set change is an instrument change; rank within one instrument), with measurement-honesty/co-published-numbers-must-reconcile for the own-lens reproduction check that withholds rows whose recompute would contradict their report.

## Summary
A fleet scan's credit reservation has no identity. The debit is written on a fresh auto:<uuid> key and its refund on ANOTHER fresh auto:<uuid> key, so nothing ties a refund to the debit it reverses; the job row's creditCharged boolean is the only record, and it is written and cleared by best-effort writes. Make the reservation a keyed ledger object - debit `scan-job:<jobId>:<attempt>`, refund `refund:<debitKey>` - and derive 'does this job hold a credit' from the ledger, exactly as the hosted lane already does.

## Description
Registry: software-engineering / cost-metering, technique `reversible-debit-and-settle` (laws creation-names-reaper, identity-survives-reuse): 'the debit hands back its own undo', 'a retry of a refunded request running the paid call for free'. The map already records this as a deviation on this exact pair. Three money defects fall out of the missing identity: (1) LOST REFUND - refundScanCredit swallows a failed grant and both callers still report creditRefunded:true, so settleJob clears creditCharged and the held credit disappears with no trace; (2) DOUBLE REFUND - a committed refund whose settle write is lost leaves creditCharged=true, the reaper requeues, the retry carries a credit that was already returned and refunds it again on a new auto key: +2 for one -1; (3) DOUBLE DEBIT - the documented kill window between reserveScanCredit and markJobCredit re-reserves. src/lib/db/hosted-credits.ts:84/137 is the in-repo proof the pattern works here.

## Flow
- consumeScanCredit gains an optional `reservationKey` (used as the debit externalId; existing auto/scan keys unchanged when absent).
- New src/lib/db/credit-reservations.ts: `scanJobReservationKey(jobId, attempt)`, `refundKeyFor(debitKey)`, `heldScanReservation(orgSlug, jobId)` = the newest `scan-job:<jobId>:*` debit with no matching `refund:` row.
- reserveScanCredit returns `reservationKey`; refundScanCredit takes it, passes `refund:<key>` as externalId, and returns `{ refunded, balance }` truthfully.
- Queue worker and import: `carriedCredit` comes from heldScanReservation (creditCharged stays as the display cache /api/org/scan/queue reads); settleJob gets creditRefunded only when the refund actually landed.
- scanCreditGate keys its hold `scan-hold:<uuid>` so the at-most-once refund is structural, not a closure boolean.
- rescan.md: delete the 'Not atomic, stated rather than hidden' residue paragraph; state the keyed reservation.

## Expected impact
No credit amount, price or charging rule moves: the same scans are charged the same one credit and refunded under the same shouldRefundScan policy. What changes is that every debit/refund pair is joinable, idempotent per reservation, and survives a lost settle, a lost refund and a mid-reserve kill.

## Evaluation
Claim: one reservation identity removes the lost-refund, double-refund and double-debit windows.
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard cases pass (2 guards green by design)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first against vitest db doubles (the existing credits.test.ts style)
Result: better
Gate: contract (ledger externalId shape for scan reservations; no schema change, no policy change)

body:
## Summary
When an org runs dry, the fleet keeps trying: every cadence and push scan that cannot reserve a credit is skipped, and a cadence skip pushes the repo a FULL cadence out. The owner who tops up sees the balance go up and nothing else; their skipped repos stay stale for a week or a month. The credits popover knows the balance, the allowance and (through ScanJob) exactly which repos were skipped - show them and resume them in one click.

## Description
Registry: software-engineering / cost-metering, technique `spend-observability` (legible while it can still change behaviour) and the plan-entitlements subject's honest-gate line; also ui-surfaces async-ui-states (a surface that reports a state should offer its exit). The paused banner is a dead end today. A pure `credit-backlog-model.ts` folds the org's recent rescore ScanJob rows to 'repos whose newest job is a credit skip' and plans a resume against balance + allowance with the same immediateScanCredits disclosure the watch flow uses. GET /api/org/credits returns the backlog only to viewers who pass requireOrgAccess (the same gate the resume POST enforces), so a read-only viewer sees no repo list. The action is the existing /api/org/scan { repos } via useOrgScanButton - no new mutation, no new price, the same per-scan charge the route already applies and caps.

## Flow
- src/lib/db/credit-backlog.ts: bounded read of rescore ScanJob rows (last 35 days, org-constrained) -> wire rows with ISO strings (added to wire-safe.ts).
- credit-backlog-model.ts: foldCreditBacklog + resumePlan (pure, red-first tests).
- route.ts: additive `creditBacklog` field behind requireOrgAccess.
- CreditsControl.backlogUi.tsx: 'N watched repos missed a scan for credits since <date>' + 'Scan N now - draws up to M credits' (or 'Top up first'); after the checkout return lands, the same section is what the owner sees next.
- billing.md: document the section; rescan.md cross-reference that a credit skip is resumable.

## Expected impact
Top-up to fresh fleet becomes one click instead of a full-cadence wait the owner cannot see. Nothing about what is charged moves: the user clicks, the existing route reserves one credit per repo beyond the allowance, exactly as Scan all does today, and the draw is disclosed before the click.

## Evaluation
Claim: the credits surface turns 'paused' into an actionable, honestly-priced backlog.
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard cases pass (1 guard green by design)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first (model unit tests, route test, component test)
Result: better
Gate: none

body:
## Summary
The app has TWO public rankings over the same public corpus, and only one of them carries the rules. `/leaderboard` reads `src/lib/register/data.ts`, which pins tenancy per query and per row and never ranks a mock floor. The landing page's board - literally titled "The register" - and /about's "real scanned public fleet" read `getPublicScanGallery` in `scans-read.ts`, which does neither: no per-row private check, an id-only extra fetch, and mock floors ranked against model scores. Make one public-corpus door and route both through it.

## Description
Applies peer-benchmarking `corpus-tenancy-boundary` ("route every corpus-building read through one door; filter per row at assembly") and `comparability-filters` ("only rows from the ranking engine enter the ranking; unknown provenance is excluded"). New `src/lib/register/corpus.ts` owns `publicCorpusWhere(orgId)`, the per-row `publicRowOrNull`, and `isRankableScan(engine)` (derived from `BENCHMARK_ELIGIBLE`, not a fourth literal). `register/data.ts` and a relocated `register/gallery.ts` both build on it; `scans-read.ts` keeps a thin re-export. The register's candidate window ranks model-scored repos in their own groupBy so mock-high repos cannot crowd them out of the 500 cap; the unranked tail gets its own bounded window. A source-scanning guard (comments/strings stripped, seeded violation) pins that every Prisma read under `src/lib/register/**` spreads `publicCorpusWhere`.

## Flow
- corpus.ts: tenancy where + per-row check + rankable predicate
- data.ts: loadCandidates uses them; verified window and preview window split
- gallery.ts: GALLERY_REPO_SELECT gains isPrivate + engineProvider; extra fetch re-asserts tenancy; topAiNative = verified only; card carries verified
- IndexGallery: demo chip on a verified:false row of the recency board
- aboutFleetModel.fleetFrom: verified only

## Expected impact
The public front door stops publishing a deterministic floor as a rank under the word "register"; a private row reaching the landing query is dropped the same way it is on /leaderboard; /about's live fleet stops being part-mock. One rule to change on the next rubric or engine decision instead of three.

## Evaluation
Claim: both public rankings enforce the same tenancy and provenance rules through one module
Before: 0 of 8 cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten (narrows what the landing board ranks; widens nothing public)

## Summary
A portfolio lead today reaches /portfolio only by URL (nothing links to it), types slugs they must already know, and gets one overall number per company with a repo count that counts mock floors the average excluded. The app already holds the viewer's readable orgs and every org's per-dimension averages. Open the page on that book, let the user toggle companies in one click, and show the company x dimension matrix with each company's weakest dimension and the book-wide gap.

## Description
New pure `src/lib/org/portfolioBookModel.ts` (`resolveBook`, `bookToggleHref`, `portfolioMatrix`). With no `?orgs`, the page seeds the book from `resolveViewerWorkspace().options` minus the public org, then re-gates EVERY slug through `canReadOrg` exactly as the typed path does - the default never widens what a viewer can read. `BookChips` renders each workspace org as an include/exclude link (plain hrefs; works without JS). `PortfolioCompany` gains `dims`, `realScoredCount`, `mockCount`; the Repos column becomes `real of scanned` with an `N mock excluded` note, per executive-reporting `denominator-naming` and the rollup's own disclosure obligation. `PortfolioMatrix` draws nine cells per company, an absent dimension as a void mark (measurement-honesty `unmeasurable-vs-zero`), the weakest one marked, and a one-line book gap ('D4 is the weakest dimension in 3 of 4 companies'). The identity menu gains 'Portfolio' when the workspace holds two or more non-public orgs.

## Flow
- Visit /portfolio signed in -> book = your readable orgs, table + matrix render immediately
- Click a chip -> that company leaves or joins the book (URL updates, shareable)
- Read the matrix -> the weakest dimension per company and across the book is named, not inferred

## Expected impact
Five steps (find URL, recall slugs, type, submit, compare one number) become one visit; the committee question 'where is the book weakest' is answered by the page, not by opening N dashboards. The repo count stops overstating the scored population.

## Evaluation
Claim: the portfolio opens on the viewer's readable book and names each company's weakest dimension with honest denominators

After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first
Result: better

## Summary
DEV_INSPECT is read raw in two places and neither carries a production floor. Give it one definition (`devInspectEnabled(env)` in a .cjs both next.config.ts and the Turbopack loader can require), with `NODE_ENV === 'production'` checked first, and pin every dev surface with a comment-stripped, seeded-violation guard.

## Description
The overlay is production-excluded at its mount (layout.tsx:80), but the build transform that stamps `data-loc="src/...:LINE:COL"` onto every host element is not: next.config.ts:100 registers it on `DEV_INSPECT === "1"` alone, and the loader's gate two (source-loc-loader.cjs:29) re-checks the same raw string. A `DEV_INSPECT=1 next build` (a copied .env, a CI job reusing a dev profile) ships source paths in every page's markup and pays Babel on every module. This is exactly the flag shape AGENTS.md forbids, and the registry technique opt-in-instrumentation-gate (agent-addressable-ui) says both gates must read one flag from one declaration (one-authority-per-vocabulary) and the transform must observe the actual invocation. The card moves the flag into one definition with the floor first, makes both gates call it, and adds one guard file for the context's three dev surfaces: no raw DEV_INSPECT read anywhere else, every /api/dev route gates with seedRequestAuthorized first (derived from the filesystem, so the next seeder is covered without a hand-list), and the overlay is only mounted behind the development check.

## Flow
- add scripts/dev-inspector/dev-inspect-flag.cjs: `devInspectEnabled(env = process.env)` -> production false, else env.DEV_INSPECT === '1'
- next.config.ts and source-loc-loader.cjs require it in place of their raw reads
- src/lib/dev/dev-inspect-flag.test.ts: definition table + loader no-op under production + next.config registration under production
- src/app/api/dev/dev-surfaces-gated.test.ts: three guards, each with a seeded violation and a prose-only non-violation
- docs/development/devinspector.md: state the floor lives in the definition

## Expected impact
A stray DEV_INSPECT on a production build becomes inert instead of leaking the source tree into shipped HTML; the dev route gate and overlay mount stop being unguarded conventions.

## Evaluation

body:
## Summary
Add a collect mode to the DevInspector: Shift+right-click (or `a` on the selected crumb) pins an element into a numbered basket that survives navigation and reload for the session; `b` copies the whole basket as one deduped, agent-pasteable list; `x` clears it.

## Description
The inspector answers 'which file is this?' one element at a time. The real request to an agent is almost always plural: 'the header chip, the empty state on /org, and the card it links to'. Today that takes a copy, a window switch and a paste per element, and anything on a second route means doing it across a navigation with the clipboard as the only memory. A pure devBasketModel.ts owns add/toggle/cap/dedupe/format/parse; useDevBasket.ts holds it in state with a try/catch sessionStorage mirror (a per-viewer convenience, never relied on); devBasketUi.tsx draws the tray (count, list, remove-one, copy, clear, the full/duplicate reason) and numbered markers on pinned elements still on screen. Lines reuse formatHudCopy, so a basket line is exactly what a single copy would produce (agent-pasteable-reference-format: one authority per vocabulary; an empty basket copies nothing and says so - failure is not an empty success). The overlay stays mounted only in development; nothing here adds a production path.

## Flow
- arm the inspector, Shift+right-click three elements (tray shows 1 2 3)
- navigate to another route, pin a fourth; reload keeps the four
- press `b`: one paste carries four `path:line` lines; HUD reports the copy rung

## Expected impact
N round trips become one paste; cross-route collection becomes possible at all.

## Evaluation
Claim: several source references can be collected across navigations and copied as one list in the same format as a single copy
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass (the guard case is green-before by design)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written red-first (model in vitest node env; keys and Shift+right-click in a jsdom dom test)
Result: better
Gate: none
